proof:
Differentiation on the compact faces gives $(A+B)'(t)=d[\int_{F_A}q(L_A^t)-\int_{F_B}q(L_B^t)]$. The sum is convex and coercive, since each endpoint cost tends to infinity on its corresponding affine lower branch as $t\to+\infty$ for $A$ or $t\to-\infty$ for $B$. Thus it has a minimizer and the two positive derivative masses agree there. The center identities follow by substituting $c_A,c_B$.

We use the triangular substitution formula proved in f6641f09c19819a3 for a bounded Borel triangular map on the open cube with positive continuous own-coordinate derivatives. Identify the planes by common orthonormal tangent coordinates with midpoint-compatible origins. For either face $F$ and density $w=q(L)$, write $W_i$ for the integral of $w$ on the section over the first $i$ coordinates, with $W_0=J$, $W_k=w$. At every interior prefix these section integrals are positive and continuous. Indeed each section has an interior lift of its prefix by convexity and projection onto the interior. Along converging interior prefixes the section indicators converge off the null boundary of the limiting section, by openness for inside points and compactness for outside points. Uniform boundedness on the compact face then gives continuity by dominated convergence. The same argument for sections truncated in the next coordinate gives continuity of the conditional CDF. The conditional density in coordinate $i$ is $W_i/W_{i-1}$ on the corresponding open interval, so inversion gives a continuous triangular map $T_F$ from $(0,1)^k$ to $\operatorname{int}F$ with diagonal derivatives $W_{i-1}/W_i$ at its respective output prefixes. Their product telescopes to $J/w(T_F)$. The substitution formula gives $(T_F)_\# dr=w\,d\mathcal H^k/J$, with $dr$ Lebesgue measure on the unit cube.

Use the common cube point $r$ to define $X=T_{F_A}(r)$, $Y=T_{F_B}(r)$, $Z=(X+Y)/2$, and let $\pi=(X,Y)_\#dr$. The midpoint map on the cube is triangular with positive diagonal derivatives, hence injective with Borel inverse on its Borel image by the same substitution formula. Write $J_Z$ for their product. Hölder's inequality on the two-term sums of the positive diagonal derivatives gives
$$
J_Z\ge J\left[\frac{q(L_A(X))^{-1/k}+q(L_B(Y))^{-1/k}}2\right]^k .
$$

For real $s_1,s_2$ with $(s_1+s_2)/2\ge\delta$ we claim
$$
f((s_1+s_2)/2)
\left[\frac{q(s_1)^{-1/k}+q(s_2)^{-1/k}}2\right]^k
\ge \frac{R(s_1)+R(s_2)}2.
$$
Put $p=(d+1)/k$. When both arguments are at least $\delta$, convexity of $s^p$ gives the inequality after division by the mean to the power $d$. If $s_1\le\delta\le s_2$, put $z=(\delta+s_2)/2$ and $b=(\delta-s_1)/2$. The mean is $z-b\ge\delta$, and convexity applied to $\delta,s_2$ bounds the left side below by $z^{d+1}/(z-b)^d$. This is at least $z+db$ by the tangent bound for $(1-b/z)^{-d}$. That is precisely the right side. The remaining case with both arguments below $\delta$ forces equality at $\delta$.

For each paired point the affine midpoint argument is $L_K(Z)=(L_A(X)+L_B(Y))/2\ge\delta$. The scalar inequality and the diagonal bound give $f(L_K(Z))J_Z\ge J(R(L_A(X))+R(L_B(Y)))/2$. Triangular substitution proves the claimed measure domination on the image of $Z$ in $F_K$, with zero transported density elsewhere. Its mass is $(A+B)/2$ by the two endpoint marginals and $qR=f$. For sharpness choose all three faces equal in one plane, with $a\ne0$ and the given denominator floor on that face. Convexity and symmetry make $t=0$ a minimizer and there the sum is exactly $2M$. The same equality occurs on each corresponding facet of three identical polytopes using a noncentroidal interior mark, whose projective normalizer is nonzero because the derivative of its objective at zero is a nonzero multiple of the centroid displacement.

statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $k=d-1$ and $\delta>0$. Put $f(s)=s^{-d}$ for $s\ge\delta$ and continue by its affine tangent for $s\le\delta$. Let $q(s)=-f'(s)/d=\max(s,\delta)^{-d-1}$ and $R(s)=f(s)/q(s)$. Thus $R(s)=s$ above $\delta$ and $R(s)=(d+1)\delta-ds$ below it. Let $F_A,F_B$ be compact convex $k$-bodies in parallel affine planes, and let $F_K$ be a compact convex $k$-body in the midpoint plane containing $(F_A+F_B)/2$. All face measures are intrinsic $\mathcal H^k$. Fix $a,y$ with $L_K(m)=1+a\cdot(m-y)\ge\delta$ on $F_K$. Put $L_A^t(x)=1+a\cdot(x-y)-t$, $L_B^t(x')=1+a\cdot(x'-y)+t$, $A(t)=\int_{F_A} f(L_A^t)$, $B(t)=\int_{F_B}f(L_B^t)$ and $M=\int_{F_K}f(L_K)$.

The minimum of $A(t)+B(t)$ is attained. At every minimizing $t$, omit its superscript and put $J=\int_{F_A}q(L_A)=\int_{F_B}q(L_B)>0$. There is one coupling $\pi$ of the probability laws $q(L_A)\,d\mathcal H^k/J$ and $q(L_B)\,d\mathcal H^k/J$, supported on $F_A\times F_B$, such that the pushforward under $(X,Y)\mapsto Z=(X+Y)/2$ satisfies
$$
\zeta=Z_\#\left(J\frac{R(L_A(X))+R(L_B(Y))}{2}\,\pi\right)\le f(L_K)\mathcal H^k|_{F_K},
\qquad
\zeta(F_K)=\frac{A(t)+B(t)}2.
$$
The midpoint map is injective on the parametrized interior coupling constructed in the proof. In particular $\min_t[A(t)+B(t)]\le 2M$, with sharp factor two even for $a\ne0$. When $a\ne0$, each $t$ is realized by physical center parameters $c_A=y+ta/\lVert a\rVert^2$, $c_B=y-ta/\lVert a\rVert^2$ with average $y$. When $a=0$ the scalar theorem permits the stated denominator offsets independently of center shifts.
title: Optimized projective facet cost with a dominated physical midpoint law
